stem:
Avni looks at the diagram of triangle $ABC$. Segment $AD$ meets side $BC$ at $D$, and the right-angle mark at $D$ is shown.

Which claim correctly names $AD$?

options.text: Call $AD$ an altitude even when $AD$ need not be perpendicular to $BC$.
Say the same segment also settles the area formula for every triangle, with no further check.
$AD$ is an altitude from $A$ to base $BC$, because it is perpendicular to $BC$.
Find $AD$ by using only that the three angles of triangle $ABC$ add to $180^{\circ}$.

teacher.key_rationale: An altitude from A to BC is the perpendicular segment from A to line BC. Dropping perpendicularity omits the defining condition. Extending the claim to every area formula over-scopes. Angle sum alone is a different mechanism.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as triangle ABC with perpendicular AD from A to BC marked as altitude.
